You are an expert in SQL. Recall how SQL treats NULL:
- A comparison with NULL (=, <>, <, >, <=, >=) yields UNKNOWN.
- NOT UNKNOWN is UNKNOWN. FALSE AND x is FALSE and TRUE OR x is TRUE for any x; otherwise AND/OR with an UNKNOWN operand yield UNKNOWN.
- WHERE and JOIN ... ON keep a row only when the condition is TRUE.
- A CHECK constraint rejects a row only when the condition is FALSE.
- x NOT IN (subquery) is UNKNOWN when x matches no value of the subquery and the subquery returns a NULL.
- SUM, MAX and other aggregates except COUNT(*) ignore NULL inputs and return NULL when every input is NULL.
